Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 7, verses 63–64:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you and that you may fear God, and perhaps you will be shown mercy?﴾ ﴿But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ark, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people.﴾

Know that His saying: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you and that you may fear God﴾ indicates that the intent of the people, in their saying to Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿Indeed, we see you in manifest error﴾, was that they attributed to him, in his claim of prophethood, error. This is for several reasons:

The first of them: they deemed it improbable that God should have a messenger to His creation, because they believed that the purpose of sending a messenger is obligation (taklif), and obligation has no benefit for the One worshipped, since He is exalted above benefit and harm, and it has no benefit for the worshipper, since in the present it entails great harm; and whatever reward is hoped for in it and the averting of punishment, God is capable of bringing about without the intermediary of obligation. Thus obligation would be vain, and God is exalted above vanity. And when obligation is invalidated, the claim of prophethood is invalidated.

The second: even though they permitted obligation, they said: "What we know to be good by reason, we do; what we know to be bad, we leave; and what we do not know, neither its goodness nor its badness, if we are compelled to it we do it, for we know that He is exalted above charging His servant with what he has no capacity for; and if we are not compelled to it, we leave it, out of caution against the danger of punishment. And since the messenger of reason is sufficient, there is no need to send another messenger."

The third: even granting that a messenger is necessary, the sending of angels is more fitting, because their awe is greater, their purity more perfect, their independence from food and drink more evident, and their distance from falsehood and vanity greater.

The fourth: even granting that He sends a messenger from among mankind, perhaps the people believed that one who is poor and has no followers or leadership does not deserve the office of messengership; and perhaps they believed that what Noah (peace be upon him) supposed to be revelation was of the kind of madness, senility, and the delusions of Satan. This is the indication to the sum of the aspects for which the disbelievers denied the messengership of a particular man. For these reasons they judged Noah to be in error. Then Noah (peace be upon him) removed their wonder and said: He, exalted is He, is the Creator of creation, so by the judgment of divinity He may command His servants regarding some matters and forbid them from others, and it is not permissible that He address them with those obligations without an intermediary, for that would lead to the limit of compulsion, which contradicts obligation. Nor is it permissible that this messenger be one of the angels, for what we mentioned in Surah al-An'am in the commentary on His saying: ﴿Had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾ [al-An'am: 9]. So it remains that the conveying of those obligations to creation is through a human being, and that human conveys those obligations to them only so that he may warn and admonish them; and when he warns them, they guard against opposing God's obligation, and when they guard against opposing God's obligation, they merit God's mercy. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿so that he may warn you, and that you may fear God, and perhaps you will be shown mercy﴾.

Having understood this, let us return to the explanation of the words of the verse.

As for His saying: ﴿Do you wonder﴾, the hamza is for censure, the waw is for conjunction, and the element conjoined to is omitted, as if it were said: "Do you deny and wonder that a reminder has come to you?" That is, you wonder that a reminder has come to you. They mentioned several interpretations of this reminder:

Al-Hasan said: it is the revelation that came to them with him. Others said: the intended reminder is the miracle, and that miracle may bear two meanings:

One: that God had sent down to him a book, and that book was a miracle, so God named it a reminder, just as He named the Qur'an by this name and made it a miracle for Muhammad (ﷺ).

The second: that this miracle was something else besides the book.

As for His saying: ﴿through a man﴾, al-Farra' said: "ʿalā" here means "maʿa" (with), as when you say: "He brought the news ʿalā its face and maʿa its face," both are permissible. Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, through the tongue of a man from among you, just as He said: ﴿Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 194], that is, through the tongue of Your messengers. Others said: ﴿a reminder from your Lord﴾ is sent down upon a man, and His saying: ﴿from among you﴾ means that you know his lineage, so he is of you by descent. This is because his being of them removes the wonder, for a person is better acquainted with one of his own kind, more knowing of the purity of his conditions, and more perceptive of what calls for tranquility toward him. Then He, exalted is He, explained the purpose for which the messenger is sent, saying: ﴿so that he may warn you﴾; the purpose of warning, saying: ﴿and that you may fear God﴾; and what they fear for, saying: ﴿and perhaps you will be shown mercy﴾. This ordering is of the utmost excellence, for the purpose of the mission is warning, the purpose of warning is guarding against everything unseemly, and the purpose of guarding is attaining mercy in the abode of the Hereafter.

Al-Jubba'i, al-Ka'bi and al-Qadi said: this verse indicates that He, exalted is He, intended from those to whom He sent the messengers piety and attainment of mercy, and this refutes the view of those who say that He intended from some of them disbelief and obstinacy, and created them for the sake of punishment and the Fire.

Our response (the Ash'aris) is: if the act does not depend on a motive, it entails the preponderance of the possible without a preponderant cause; and if it depends on it, it entails compulsion (jabr). And whenever that follows, it is necessary to be certain that He intended disbelief from the disbeliever, and this refutes your doctrine. Then He, exalted is He, explained that, despite this, they denied him in his claim of prophethood and his conveying of obligations from God, and persisted in that denial. Then He, exalted is He, saved him in the ark, and saved those with him among the believers, and drowned the disbelievers and the deniers. He explained the cause of this, saying: ﴿Indeed, they were a blind people﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: their hearts became blind to the knowledge of tawhid, prophethood and the return. The lexicographers said: one says a man is ʿamin in insight and aʿma in sight. God the Exalted said: ﴿Then the news became obscure to them that day﴾ [al-Qasas: 66], and He said: ﴿Clear proofs have come to you from your Lord; so whoever sees, it is for his own soul, and whoever is blind, it is against it﴾ [al-An'am: 104]. Zuhayr said:

I know what is in today and yesterday before it, but as for knowledge of what is in tomorrow, I am blind.

The author of al-Kashshaf said: it was read ʿāmīn (ʿāmīn). The difference between ʿamī and ʿāmī is that ʿamī indicates a established blindness, and ʿāmī indicates a newly arisen blindness. There is no doubt that their blindness was established and firmly rooted, and the evidence for this is His saying in another verse: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36].

God Most High says: ﴿And to ʿĀd We sent their brother Hūd. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary of Him?"﴾ ﴿The eminent ones among his people who disbelieved said, "Indeed we see you in folly, and indeed we think you are among the liars."﴾ ﴿He said, "O my people, there is no folly in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am a sincere, trustworthy adviser to you.﴾ ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, to warn you? And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah, and increased you in stature and bodily build. So remember the bounties of God that you may prosper."﴾

Know that this is the second story, the story of Hūd with his people.

[p. 126 continued]

As for His saying: ﴿And to ʿĀd We sent their brother Hūd﴾, there are several discussions:

The first discussion: His saying "their brother" (akhāhum) is governed in the accusative by His saying "We sent" (arsalnā) at the beginning of the speech, the implied sense being: "We had indeed sent Noah to his people, and We sent to ʿĀd their brother Hūd."

The second discussion: They agreed that Hūd was not their brother in religion. They differed as to whether he was a brother by close kinship or not. Al-Kalbī said: he was one of that tribe. Others said: he was of the children of Adam and of their kind, not of the kind of the angels. This degree is sufficient for calling this relationship "brotherhood." The meaning is that We sent to ʿĀd one of their own kind, a human being, so that familiarity and intimacy with his words and deeds would be more complete. We did not send to them a person of a different kind, such as a king or a jinn.

The third discussion: "Their brother" means their companion and messenger. The Arabs call the companion of a people "the brother of the people." From this is His saying: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 38], meaning its companion and counterpart. And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the brother of Ṣudāʾ has called the adhān, and whoever calls the adhān is the one to establish it," meaning their companion.

The fourth discussion: They said: the lineage of this Hūd is: Hūd son of Shālakh, son of Arfakhshadh, son of Sām, son of Noah. As for ʿĀd, they were a people in Yemen, in al-Aḥqāf. Ibn Isḥāq said: al-Aḥqāf is the sand dunes that lie between ʿUmān and Ḥaḍramawt.

The fifth discussion: Know that the wording of this story agrees with the wording mentioned in the story of Noah (peace be upon him), except in some matters:

The first: In the story of Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿So he said, "O my people, worship God"﴾, and in the story of Hūd: ﴿He said, "O my people, worship God"﴾. The difference is that Noah (peace be upon him) was constant in calling his people and did not delay his reply to their doubts for a single moment, whereas Hūd's insistence did not reach this degree. Therefore the particle of sequence (fāʾ al-taʿqīb, the "fa" indicating immediate succession) came in Noah's speech and not in Hūd's.

The second: In the story of Noah he said: ﴿Worship God; you have no god other than Him. Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day﴾, and in this story he said: ﴿Worship God; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary?﴾ The difference between the two forms is that before Noah no such great event had occurred in the world as the mighty Flood. Therefore Noah informed them of that event, saying: ﴿Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day﴾. As for the event of Hūd (peace be upon him), it was preceded by the event of Noah, and people still had recent knowledge of that event. Therefore Hūd was content with saying: ﴿Will you not then be wary?﴾ The meaning is: you know that when the people of Noah did not fear God and did not obey Him, that punishment befell them, whose report became famous in the world. So His saying ﴿Will you not then be wary?﴾ is an allusion to warning them with that earlier, well-known event in the world.

The third difference: God Most High said in the story of Noah: ﴿The eminent ones of his people said﴾, and in the story of Hūd: ﴿The eminent ones among his people who disbelieved said﴾. The difference is that among the nobles of Hūd's people there were those who believed in him, among them Marthad ibn Saʿd, who embraced Islam but used to conceal his faith. So the distinction was intended by means of the description. Among the nobles of Noah's people there was no believer.

The fourth difference: God Most High related of Noah's people that they said: ﴿Indeed we see you in manifest error﴾, and related of Hūd's people that they said: ﴿Indeed we see you in folly, and indeed we think you are among the liars﴾. The difference between the two cases is that Noah (peace be upon him) was warning the disbelievers of the general Flood, and was also occupied with building the ark, and needed to exert himself in building it. At this, the people said: ﴿Indeed we see you in manifest error﴾, and no sign had appeared of the things that indicate the coming of water in that wilderness. As for Hud, peace be upon him, his saying ﴿and I am a trustworthy adviser to you﴾ indicates that he was firm and settled in that counsel. As for the other difference in this verse, namely that Noah, peace be upon him, said ﴿and I know from God what you do not know﴾, while Hud described himself as trustworthy, the difference is that Noah, peace be upon him, was higher in rank and greater in station in prophethood than Hud. **Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 7, verses 70–72:**

**His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: "Have you come to us so that we worship God alone and abandon what our fathers used to worship? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful."﴾ ﴿He said: "Indeed there has befallen you from your Lord an abomination (rijs) and wrath. Know that this is the third story, and it is the story of Salih.

As for His saying, ﴿And to Thamud﴾, the meaning is: "And We certainly sent Noah, and to 'Ad their brother Hud, and to Thamud their brother Salih." And in this there are issues:

The first issue: Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: Thamud was named for the scarcity of its water, from al-thamd, which is the little water. Their dwellings were al-Hijr, between the Hijaz and al-Sham, extending to Wadi al-Qura. It was also said: Thamud was named after their eldest forefather, who was Thamud ibn 'Ad ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Noah, upon him be peace.

The second issue: "And to Thamud" was read with non-declension (ghayr munsarif) by interpreting it as the tribe, and "And to Thamudin" with declension by interpreting it as the group, or by considering the original (al-asl), since it is the name of their eldest forefather. The Qur'an has come with both explicitly. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Unquestionably, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. Unquestionably, away with Thamud!﴾ [Hud: 68].

Know that He, may He be exalted, related of him that he commanded them to worship Allah and forbade them from worshipping other than Allah, as was mentioned of the prophets before him.

* * *
Then He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord﴾. This addition is mentioned in this story, and it indicates that every prophet before him used to cite proofs for the soundness of monotheism and prophethood, because mere imitation alone, if it were sufficient, would make that clear evidence here pointless. Then He explained that this clear evidence is the she-camel, so He said: ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you﴾. In this there are issues:

The first issue: They mentioned that when Allah destroyed 'Ad, Thamud took their place, their lifespans were long, and their luxury increased. Then they disobeyed Allah and worshipped idols. So Allah sent to them Salih, who was one of them, and they demanded of him a miracle. He said: "What do you want?" They said: "You will come out with us on our festival, and we will bring out our idols; you will ask your god, and we will ask our idols. If the effect of your supplication appears, we will follow you, and if the effect of our supplication appears, you will follow us." So he went out with them. They asked him to bring forth for them a great she-camel from a specific rock, and he took their covenants that if he did so they would believe, and they accepted. He prayed two rak'ahs and called upon Allah, and that rock quaked as a pregnant woman quakes, then it split open and the she-camel emerged from its midst. She was of extreme size, and water was scarce among them, so they made that water entirely a drink for her on one day, and on the second day a drink for the whole people. Al-Suddi said: On the day she drank the water, she would pass between the two mountains, rising over them, then come and drink, and she would milk enough for everyone, as if she were pouring out milk. On the day they drank the water, she would not come to them, and she had with her a young camel. Salih said to them: "A boy will be born in this month of yours, by whose hands your destruction will come." So nine men among them slaughtered their sons, then the tenth was born, and his father refused to slaughter him. He grew up rapidly, and when he became a grown youth he sat with a group who were drinking wine, and they wanted water to mix with it, but it was the day of the she-camel's drinking, and they could not find water, and this distressed them. The youth said: "Shall I hamstring this she-camel for you?" He attacked her, and when she saw him she charged at him, and he fled from her behind a rock, and they corralled her for him. When she passed by him, he seized her and hamstrung her, and she fell. This is His saying: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took it and hamstrung it﴾ [al-Qamar: 29]. At that point they showed their disbelief and transgressed the command of their Lord. Then Salih said to them: "The sign of the punishment is that you will become red tomorrow, and the day after yellow, and the third day black." When the punishment dawned upon them, they perfumed themselves with camphor and prepared themselves.

Having known this, we say: The scholars differed regarding the manner in which the she-camel was a sign. Some of them said: It was a sign because of her emergence in her entirety from the rock. Al-Qadi said: This, if it is authentic, is miraculous in several respects:

One: her emergence from the mountain.

The second: that she was not from a male and female.

The third: the perfection of her creation without gradual development.

The second view: It was a sign only because she had a day's drink, and all of Thamud had a day's drink, and for a single she-camel to take the drink of a whole nation is remarkable; moreover, she would bring forth what suits that water of pasture and herbage.

The third view: The aspect of the miracle in her was that on the day of her drinking they would milk from her the amount that stood in place of water for them on their drinking day. Al-Hasan said the opposite of that, saying: she never gave a single drop of milk, and this statement contradicts what preceded it.

The fourth view: The aspect of the miracle in her was that on the day she came to the water, all the animals refrained from coming down to the water, and on the day she refrained, the animals would come.

Know that the Qur'an has indicated that there was a sign in her, but as for mention of in which respects she was a sign, it is not stated. Knowledge is attained that she was a miracle in some respect without doubt, and Allah knows best.

* * *

The second issue: His saying: ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you﴾. Here, "as a sign" (ayatan) is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: she is pointed to while being a sign. The word "this" (hadhihi) carries the sense of pointing, and "sign" (ayah) carries the sense of "indicating"; therefore it is permissible for it to be a circumstantial clause.
If it is said: That she-camel was a sign for everyone, so why did He single out those peoples by saying: ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you﴾?

We say: In this there are several aspects:

One: they saw her directly, and others were informed about her, and report is not like direct witnessing.

Second: Perhaps He had established all the other miracles, but the people asked him for this very miracle as a demand, so Allah manifested it for them; for this reason the singling out is apt.

If it is said: What is the benefit in singling out that she-camel as "the she-camel of Allah"?

We say: In this there are several aspects:

It was said: He attributed her to Allah as an honour and distinction, like His saying: the House of Allah.

It was said: Because He created her without intermediary.

It was said: Because there is no owner of her other than Allah.

It was said: Because she is Allah's proof against the people.

* * *
Then He said: ﴿So leave her to eat within the earth of Allah﴾, meaning the earth is the earth of Allah, and the she-camel is the she-camel of Allah; so leave her to eat in the land of her Lord. The land does not belong to you, nor what is in it of plants by your growing them. ﴿And do not touch her with harm﴾: do not strike her, do not drive her away, and do not approach her with any kind of harm. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "O 'Ali, the most wretched of the first ones was the slayer of Salih's she-camel, and the most wretched of the last ones is your slayer."

* * *
Then Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad﴾. It was said: When Allah destroyed 'Ad, Thamud resettled their lands and succeeded them in the earth, multiplied, and lived long lifespans.

* * *
Then He said: ﴿and settled you in the land﴾, meaning He housed you; al-mubawwa' is the dwelling place in the land, that is, in the land of al-Hijr between the Hijaz and al-Sham.

* * *
Then He said: ﴿taking from its plains palaces﴾, meaning you settle in palaces from the levelness of the land, for palaces are built only from clay, mud bricks, and baked brick, and these materials are made only from the levelness of the land. ﴿And carving out the mountains as homes﴾, meaning you carve out homes from the mountains, roofing them.
If they say: Over what is "homes" (buyutan) in the accusative?

We say: It is in the circumstantial accusative, as one says: "He sewed this cloth as a shirt," and "He pared this reed as a pen," and this is the accusative of anticipated state (al-hal al-muqaddarah), because a mountain is not a house during carving, nor is the cloth a shirt or the reed a pen during sewing and paring. It was also said: They used to inhabit the plains in summer and the mountains in winter, and this indicates that they were luxurious and affluent.

* * *
Then He said: ﴿So remember the bounties of Allah﴾, meaning: I have mentioned to you some categories of the blessings Allah has given you, and mentioning all of them is lengthy; so remember, by your intellects, what is in them. ﴿And do not commit abuse on the earth, causing corruption﴾. It was said: What is meant by it is the prohibition against hamstringing the she-camel, and the better view is to take it in its apparent sense, which is the prohibition of every kind of corruption.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 7, verse 73–74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you, so leave her to eat within the earth of Allah, and do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment seize you."﴾ ﴿And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad and settled you in the land, taking from its plains palaces and carving out the mountains as homes. So remember the bounties of Allah and do not commit abuse on the earth, causing corruption.﴾

Know that this is the third story, and it is the story of Salih.

As for His saying, ﴿And to Thamud﴾, the meaning is: "And We certainly sent Noah, and to 'Ad their brother Hud, and to Thamud their brother Salih." And in this there are issues:

The first issue: Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: Thamud was named for the scarcity of its water, from al-thamd, which is the little water. Their dwellings were al-Hijr, between the Hijaz and al-Sham, extending to Wadi al-Qura. It was also said: Thamud was named after their eldest forefather, who was Thamud ibn 'Ad ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Noah, upon him be peace.

The second issue: "And to Thamud" was read with non-declension (ghayr munsarif) by interpreting it as the tribe, and "And to Thamudin" with declension by interpreting it as the group, or by considering the original (al-asl), since it is the name of their eldest forefather. The Qur'an has come with both explicitly. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Unquestionably, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. Unquestionably, away with Thamud!﴾ [Hud: 68].

Know that He, may He be exalted, related of him that he commanded them to worship Allah and forbade them from worshipping other than Allah, as was mentioned of the prophets before him.

* * *
Then He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord﴾. This addition is mentioned in this story, and it indicates that every prophet before him used to cite proofs for the soundness of monotheism and prophethood, because mere imitation alone, if it were sufficient, would make that clear evidence here pointless. Then He explained that this clear evidence is the she-camel, so He said: ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you﴾. In this there are issues:

The first issue: They mentioned that when Allah destroyed 'Ad, Thamud took their place, their lifespans were long, and their luxury increased. Then they disobeyed Allah and worshipped idols. So Allah sent to them Salih, who was one of them, and they demanded of him a miracle. He said: "What do you want?" They said: "You will come out with us on our festival, and we will bring out our idols; you will ask your god, and we will ask our idols. If the effect of your supplication appears, we will follow you, and if the effect of our supplication appears, you will follow us." So he went out with them. They asked him to bring forth for them a great she-camel from a specific rock, and he took their covenants that if he did so they would believe, and they accepted. He prayed two rak'ahs and called upon Allah, and that rock quaked as a pregnant woman quakes, then it split open and the she-camel emerged from its midst. She was of extreme size, and water was scarce among them, so they made that water entirely a drink for her on one day, and on the second day a drink for the whole people. Al-Suddi said: On the day she drank the water, she would pass between the two mountains, rising over them, then come and drink, and she would milk enough for everyone, as if she were pouring out milk. On the day they drank the water, she would not come to them, and she had with her a young camel. Salih said to them: "A boy will be born in this month of yours, by whose hands your destruction will come." So nine men among them slaughtered their sons, then the tenth was born, and his father refused to slaughter him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The eminent ones of his people who were arrogant said to those who were deemed weak, to those among them who believed: "Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" They said: "Indeed, we believe in what he has been sent with."﴾ ﴿Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have believed."﴾ ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel, and they defied the command of their Lord, and they said: "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers."﴾ ﴿So the violent quake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homeland.﴾ ﴿Then he turned away from them and said: "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely, but you do not love those who give sincere advice."﴾

Know that we have mentioned that al-mala' (the chiefs, the notables) is a term for the people whose hearts are filled with awe of them. The meaning of the verse is: "The chiefs, who were arrogant among his people, said to those who were deemed weak," meaning the poor people who believed in him. His saying ﴿to those among them who believed﴾ is a substitution (badal) for his saying ﴿to those who were deemed weak﴾, because they are the believers. Know that He described those disbelievers as arrogant, and described those believers as weak. Their being arrogant is an act for which they deserve blame. The believers being weak means that others oppress and belittle them; this is not an act issuing from them but from others. Therefore it is not a description of blame concerning them; rather, the blame returns to those who belittle and oppress them.

Then Allah the Exalted related that these arrogant ones asked the weak ones about the condition of Salih. The weak ones said: "We are certain and we affirm what Salih has brought." The arrogant ones said: "Rather, we disbelieve in what Salih has brought." This verse is among the greatest proofs used to demonstrate that poverty is better than wealth. This is because arrogance arises only from abundance of wealth and status, while being belittled arises only from their scarcity. Allah the Exalted made clear that abundance of wealth and status led them to rebellion, refusal, denial and disbelief, while scarcity of wealth and status led them to faith, affirmation and submission. This indicates that poverty is better than wealth.

* * *

Then Allah said: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel.﴾ Al-Azhari said: al-'aqr (hamstringing) among the Arabs is cutting the hamstring of a camel. Since hamstringing was a cause of slaughtering, al-'aqr was applied to slaughtering, using the name of the cause for the effect. Know that He attributed the hamstringing to all of them, because it occurred with their consent, even though only some of them actually carried it out. It is said to a great tribe: "You did such-and-such," even though only one of them did it.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and they defied the command of their Lord.﴾ It is said: 'ata yata'tu 'utuwwan, when he became arrogant. From this it is said: jabbarun 'ati (a tyrant who is defiant). Mujahid said: al-'utuww is excessiveness in falsehood. Regarding His saying ﴿against the command of their Lord﴾ there are two possibilities:

The first: the meaning is: they were arrogant against carrying out the command of their Lord, and that command is what Allah conveyed to them through Salih, peace be upon him, namely His saying: ﴿Leave her to eat in the land of Allah.﴾

The second: the meaning is: their defiance issued from the command of their Lord. It is as if the command of their Lord to leave her became a cause for their proceeding to that defiance, just as it is said: "The forbidden is followed." ﴿And they said: "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers."﴾ They only said this because they were denying him regarding everything he reported concerning promise and threat.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So the violent quake seized them.﴾ Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: ar-rajfah is a severe earthquake. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the day when the earth and the mountains quake, and the mountains become a heap of sand poured out﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14]. Al-Layth said: It is said: raja/a ash-shay'u yarjufu rajfan wa rajafanan, like the trembling of a camel beneath its saddle, and as a tree trembles when the wind shakes it.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿So they became prostrate in their homeland.﴾ That is, in their land; that is why He used the singular "dar" (home/abode), as one says: "dar al-harb" (the land of war), and "I passed by the dar of the cloth-merchants." In another verse He used the plural and said: ﴿in their homes﴾ [Hud: 67], because by dar he meant what belongs to each one of them, his own particular dwelling. His saying ﴿prostrate﴾ — Abu 'Ubayda said: al-judum (crouching, lying prostrate) for people and birds is like al-buruk (kneeling) for camels. The crouching of a bird is its settling flat on the ground while it is still at night. The meaning is: they became prostrate, motionless, dead, not moving. It is said: "The people are jathm," that is, sitting, without any movement and without perceiving anything. From this comes al-mujaththamah, which is forbidden: it is an animal that is tied up to be shot. Thus it is established that al-judum is an expression for stillness and lifelessness. Then they differed. Some said: when they heard the tremendous cry, their hearts broke and they died prostrate on their knees. It was also said: rather, they fell on their faces. It was also said: the thunderbolt reached them and they burned and became like ash. It was also said: rather, at the descent of the punishment upon them some fell on others. All of these are close in meaning.

Here there are questions:

The first question: when He related of them that they said: ﴿O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers,﴾ He said: ﴿So the violent quake seized them,﴾ and the particle fa' indicates immediate sequence. This implies that the quake seized them immediately after they uttered that statement, but this is not the case, because He said in another verse: ﴿So he said: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied."﴾ [Hud: 65].

The answer: what occurs a short time after something may still be said to occur after it, and so the question is dispelled.

The second question: some heretics criticized these verses, claiming that the words of the Qur'an differ in narrating this event: ar-rajfah, at-tagiyah, and as-sayhah. They claimed that this necessitates contradiction.

The answer: Abu Muslim said: at-tagiyah is a name for anything that exceeds its limit, whether it is an animate being or not, and the ha' is attached to it for emphasis. Muslims call a tyrannical king at-taghiyah and at-taghut. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, man does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6–7]. It is said: taghā yatghā tughyānan, and he is tāghin and tāghiyah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thamud denied through their rebellion﴾ [ash-Shams: 11], and He said about non-animate things: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose beyond its measure﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11], that is, it overcame and exceeded its limit. As for ar-rajfah, it is an earthquake in the land, a movement outside the usual. So it is not far-fetched to apply the name at-tagiyah to it. As for as-sayhah, it is generally the case that an earthquake is not separated from a tremendous, terrifying cry. As for as-sā'iqah (the thunderbolt), it is generally an earthquake, and likewise az-zajrah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is only one shout﴾ ﴿and behold, they are on the surface [of the earth]﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 13–14]. Thus what the critic said is refuted.

[p. 136]

The third question: the people witnessed the she-camel emerging from the rock, and that is an overpowering miracle that brings the state of those obligated near to compulsion (ilja') when they witness such a miracle. Also they witnessed that the water which was the drinking-share of all those peoples on one day became the drinking-share of that single she-camel on the second day, and that too is an overpowering miracle. Then, when they slaughtered her, and Salih, peace be upon him, had threatened them with a severe punishment if they slaughtered her, after they proceeded to slaughter her they witnessed the signs of punishment, which is what is reported: they turned red on the first day, then yellow on the second day, then black on the third day. So, with the witnessing of those overpowering miracles at the beginning of the matter, and then witnessing the descent of severe punishment at the end of the matter, is it conceivable that a sane person would remain insistent upon his disbelief, not repenting from it?

The first answer is to say: before they witnessed those signs, they used to deny Salih regarding the descent of the punishment; but when they witnessed the signs, they at that point went beyond the limit of obligation, and their repentance was no longer accepted.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So he turned away from them.﴾ There are two views concerning this:

The first: he turned away from them after they had died. The evidence for this is that He said: ﴿So they became prostrate in their homeland﴾ ﴿So he turned away from them,﴾ and the particle fa' indicates immediate sequence, so this turning away is shown to have occurred after their prostration.

The second: he, peace be upon him, turned away from them before their death, as evidenced by the fact that he addressed the people and said: ﴿O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely, but you do not love those who give sincere advice.﴾ This indicates that they were alive, for three reasons:

The first: he said to them, "O my people," and the dead are not described as a people, because the derivation of the word qawm is from standing independently, and that is absent in the case of the dead.

The second: these words are addressed to those people, and addressing the dead is not permissible.

The third: he said: ﴿but you do not love those who give sincere advice,﴾ so it must be that they are in a state in which love can occur in them.

It may be answered: a man may say to his friend, who is dead, and whom he had advised but who did not accept that advice until he cast himself into destruction: "O my brother, how long have I advised you and you did not accept, and how often have I forbidden you and you did not refrain? So it is here." The benefit of mentioning this statement is either that some of the living may hear it, take heed from it, and be restrained from that same course; or that his heart was burned by that event, and when he mentioned those words, that matter was relieved from his heart. It was said: the effect of that calamity lightens for him. They also mentioned another answer, which is: Salih, peace be upon him, addressed them after they had become prostrate, just as our Prophet (ﷺ) addressed the slain of Badr. It was said to him: "Do you speak to these corpses?" He said: "You are no better at hearing than they are, but they are unable to answer."

They also mentioned another answer, which is: Salih, peace be upon him, addressed them after they had become prostrate, just as our Prophet (ﷺ) addressed the slain of Badr. It was said to him: "Do you speak to these corpses?" He said: "You are no better at hearing than they are, but they are unable to answer."

[p. 135]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The eminent ones of his people who were arrogant said to those who were deemed weak, to those among them who believed: "Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" They said: "Indeed, we believe in what he has been sent with."﴾ ﴿Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have believed."﴾ ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel, and they defied the command of their Lord, and they said: "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers."﴾ ﴿So the violent quake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homeland.﴾ ﴿Then he turned away from them and said: "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely, but you do not love those who give sincere advice."﴾

Know that we have mentioned that al-mala' (the chiefs, the notables) is a term for the people whose hearts are filled with awe of them. The meaning of the verse is: "The chiefs, who were arrogant among his people, said to those who were deemed weak," meaning the poor people who believed in him. His saying ﴿to those among them who believed﴾ is a substitution (badal) for his saying ﴿to those who were deemed weak﴾, because they are the believers. Know that He described those disbelievers as arrogant, and described those believers as weak. Their being arrogant is an act for which they deserve blame. The believers being weak means that others oppress and belittle them; this is not an act issuing from them but from others. Therefore it is not a description of blame concerning them; rather, the blame returns to those who belittle and oppress them.

Then Allah the Exalted related that these arrogant ones asked the weak ones about the condition of Salih. The weak ones said: "We are certain and we affirm what Salih has brought." The arrogant ones said: "Rather, we disbelieve in what Salih has brought." This verse is among the greatest proofs used to demonstrate that poverty is better than wealth. This is because arrogance arises only from abundance of wealth and status, while being belittled arises only from their scarcity. Allah the Exalted made clear that abundance of wealth and status led them to rebellion, refusal, denial and disbelief, while scarcity of wealth and status led them to faith, affirmation and submission. This indicates that poverty is better than wealth.

* * *

Then Allah said: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel.﴾ Al-Azhari said: al-'aqr (hamstringing) among the Arabs is cutting the hamstring of a camel. Since hamstringing was a cause of slaughtering, al-'aqr was applied to slaughtering, using the name of the cause for the effect. Know that He attributed the hamstringing to all of them, because it occurred with their consent, even though only some of them actually carried it out. It is said to a great tribe: "You did such-and-such," even though only one of them did it.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and they defied the command of their Lord.﴾ It is said: 'ata yata'tu 'utuwwan, when he became arrogant. From this it is said: jabbarun 'ati (a tyrant who is defiant). Mujahid said: al-'utuww is excessiveness in falsehood. Regarding His saying ﴿against the command of their Lord﴾ there are two possibilities:

The first: the meaning is: they were arrogant against carrying out the command of their Lord, and that command is what Allah conveyed to them through Salih, peace be upon him, namely His saying: ﴿Leave her to eat in the land of Allah.﴾

The second: the meaning is: their defiance issued from the command of their Lord. It is as if the command of their Lord to leave her became a cause for their proceeding to that defiance, just as it is said: "The forbidden is followed." ﴿And they said: "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers."﴾ They only said this because they were denying him regarding everything he reported concerning promise and threat.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So the violent quake seized them.﴾ Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: ar-rajfah is a severe earthquake. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the day when the earth and the mountains quake, and the mountains become a heap of sand poured out﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14]. Al-Layth said: It is said: raja/a ash-shay'u yarjufu rajfan wa rajafanan, like the trembling of a camel beneath its saddle, and as a tree trembles when the wind shakes it.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿So they became prostrate in their homeland.﴾ That is, in their land; that is why He used the singular "dar" (home/abode), as one says: "dar al-harb" (the land of war), and "I passed by the dar of the cloth-merchants." In another verse He used the plural and said: ﴿in their homes﴾ [Hud: 67], because by dar he meant what belongs to each one of them, his own particular dwelling. His saying ﴿prostrate﴾ — Abu 'Ubayda said: al-judum (crouching, lying prostrate) for people and birds is like al-buruk (kneeling) for camels. The crouching of a bird is its settling flat on the ground while it is still at night. The meaning is: they became prostrate, motionless, dead, not moving. It is said: "The people are jathm," that is, sitting, without any movement and without perceiving anything. From this comes al-mujaththamah, which is forbidden: it is an animal that is tied up to be shot. Thus it is established that al-judum is an expression for stillness and lifelessness. Then they differed. Some said: when they heard the tremendous cry, their hearts broke and they died prostrate on their knees. It was also said: rather, they fell on their faces. It was also said: the thunderbolt reached them and they burned and became like ash. It was also said: rather, at the descent of the punishment upon them some fell on others. All of these are close in meaning.

Here there are questions:

The first question: when He related of them that they said: ﴿O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers,﴾ He said: ﴿So the violent quake seized them,﴾ and the particle fa' indicates immediate sequence. This implies that the quake seized them immediately after they uttered that statement, but this is not the case, because He said in another verse: ﴿So he said: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied."﴾ [Hud: 65].

The answer: what occurs a short time after something may still be said to occur after it, and so the question is dispelled.

The second question: some heretics criticized these verses, claiming that the words of the Qur'an differ in narrating this event: ar-rajfah, at-tagiyah, and as-sayhah. They claimed that this necessitates contradiction.

The answer: Abu Muslim said: at-tagiyah is a name for anything that exceeds its limit, whether it is an animate being or not, and the ha' is attached to it for emphasis. Muslims call a tyrannical king at-taghiyah and at-taghut. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, man does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6–7]. It is said: taghā yatghā tughyānan, and he is tāghin and tāghiyah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thamud denied through their rebellion﴾ [ash-Shams: 11], and He said about non-animate things: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose beyond its measure﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11], that is, it overcame and exceeded its limit. As for ar-rajfah, it is an earthquake in the land, a movement outside the usual. So it is not far-fetched to apply the name at-tagiyah to it. As for as-sayhah, it is generally the case that an earthquake is not separated from a tremendous, terrifying cry. As for as-sā'iqah (the thunderbolt), it is generally an earthquake, and likewise az-zajrah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is only one shout﴾ ﴿and behold, they are on the surface [of the earth]﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 13–14]. Thus what the critic said is refuted.

[p. 136]

The third question: the people witnessed the she-camel emerging from the rock, and that is an overpowering miracle that brings the state of those obligated near to compulsion (ilja') when they witness such a miracle. Also they witnessed that the water which was the drinking-share of all those peoples on one day became the drinking-share of that single she-camel on the second day, and that too is an overpowering miracle. Then, when they slaughtered her, and Salih, peace be upon him, had threatened them with a severe punishment if they slaughtered her, after they proceeded to slaughter her they witnessed the signs of punishment, which is what is reported: they turned red on the first day, then yellow on the second day, then black on the third day. So, with the witnessing of those overpowering miracles at the beginning of the matter, and then witnessing the descent of severe punishment at the end of the matter, is it conceivable that a sane person would remain insistent upon his disbelief, not repenting from it?

The first answer is to say: before they witnessed those signs, they used to deny Salih regarding the descent of the punishment; but when they witnessed the signs, they at that point went beyond the limit of obligation, and their repentance was no longer accepted.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So he turned away from them.﴾ There are two views concerning this:

The first: he turned away from them after they had died. The evidence for this is that He said: ﴿So they became prostrate in their homeland﴾ ﴿So he turned away from them,﴾ and the particle fa' indicates immediate sequence, so this turning away is shown to have occurred after their prostration.

The second: he, peace be upon him, turned away from them before their death, as evidenced by the fact that he addressed the people and said: ﴿O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely, but you do not love those who give sincere advice.﴾ This indicates that they were alive, for three reasons:

The first: he said to them, "O my people," and the dead are not described as a people, because the derivation of the word qawm is from standing independently, and that is absent in the case of the dead.

The second: these words are addressed to those people, and addressing the dead is not permissible.

The third: he said: ﴿but you do not love those who give sincere advice,﴾ so it must be that they are in a state in which love can occur in them.

It may be answered: a man may say to his friend, who is dead, and whom he had advised but who did not accept that advice until he cast himself into destruction: "O my brother, how long have I advised you and you did not accept, and how often have I forbidden you and you did not refrain? So it is here." The benefit of mentioning this statement is either that some of the living may hear it, take heed from it, and be restrained from that same course; or that his heart was burned by that event, and when he mentioned those words, that matter was relieved from his heart. It was said: the effect of that calamity lightens for him. They also mentioned another answer, which is: Salih, peace be upon him, addressed them after they had become prostrate, just as our Prophet (ﷺ) addressed the slain of Badr. It was said to him: "Do you speak to these corpses?" He said: "You are no better at hearing than they are, but they are unable to answer."

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 7, verse 80:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [We sent] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit an indecency that no one in the worlds has preceded you in?"﴾

Know that this is the fourth story. The grammarians (al-nahwiyyun) said: Lot was not diptotic (lam yunsarif) [i.e., he takes tanwin] only because of his lightness, for he is composed of three letters and has a quiescent middle letter. ﴿Do you commit the indecency?﴾ Do you do the evil deed that persists in ugliness? As for His saying, ﴿that no one in the worlds has preceded you in?﴾, there are two discussions:

First discussion: The author of al-Kashshaf said: The first "min" (in min ahadin) is superfluous, for emphasizing the negation and conveying the meaning of comprehensiveness, while the second "min" (in min al-alamin) is partitive.

If it is asked: How is it permissible to say, ﴿that no one in the worlds has preceded you in?﴾ when desire always calls to that act?

The answer: We see many people who find that act disgusting. Since it is possible that many people find it disgusting, it is not far-fetched that many ages may pass in which none of the people of those ages undertakes it. There is also another answer, which is to say: Perhaps they all, collectively, turned to that act, and total devotion to that act is something that did not exist in earlier ages. Al-Hasan said: They used to have intercourse with men in their backsides, and they used to have intercourse only with strangers. ʿAtaʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbas: That practice became entrenched among them, until some of them did it to others.

Second discussion: His saying, ﴿that no one has preceded you in?﴾ may be a resumed (mustaʾnaf) statement of rebuke to them, and it may be an attribute of the indecency, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day﴾ [Yasin: 37], and the poet said:

"And indeed I pass by the base man, and he insults me..."

Then He said: ﴿Indeed you approach men lustfully, instead of women. Rather, you are a people who exceed limits.﴾

There are several issues here:

First issue: Nafi' and Hafs, from 'Asim, read "innakum" with a kasra on the alif (إنَّكم). The method of Nafi' is to dispense with the second interrogative and keep only the first in the whole Qur'an. Ibn Kathir read "a'innakum" (أئِنَّكم) with a non-elongated hamza and an intermediate pronunciation between the second hamza and the alif. Abu 'Amr read it with an elongated hamza, with lightening, and an intermediate pronunciation of the second. The rest read it with two hamzas according to the original form. Al-Wahidi said: whoever reads it as an interrogative, this is an interrogative meaning denial, due to His saying: ﴿Do you commit the abomination?﴾ and each of the two interrogatives is an independent sentence that does not need anything to complete it.

Second issue: His saying: ﴿shahwatan﴾ (شَهْوَةً) is a verbal noun (maṣdar). Abu Zayd said: shahiya yashha shahwatan, and its being in the accusative is as a verbal noun, because His saying ﴿you approach men﴾ means "Do you desire with desire?" If you wish, you may say it is a verbal noun that occupies the position of a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl).

Third issue: In explaining the reasons that make this act ugly.

Know that the ugliness of this act is like a matter established in natures, so there is no need to enumerate the reasons in detail. Then we say the causes of its ugliness are many:

The first of them: most people guard against the existence of offspring, because its existence drives a person to seek wealth and exhaust the self in earning, but He, exalted, made intercourse a cause of obtaining great pleasure, such that a person, in seeking that pleasure, proceeds to intercourse, and then offspring comes into being whether he wills it or not. By this way the progeny remains and the species does not cease. So He placed the pleasure in intercourse, like a man who sets a trap for some animals, for he must place in that trap something the animal desires so that it becomes the cause of its falling into that trap. The placing of pleasure in intercourse resembles placing what the animal desires in the trap, and the purpose of it is the preservation of the human species, which is the noblest of species.

Having established this, we say: if a person could obtain that pleasure by a means that does not lead to offspring, the wisdom sought would not be achieved, and that would lead to the cessation of progeny, and that is contrary to the ruling of God. Therefore it is necessary to rule its prohibition decisively, until that pleasure is obtained by the way that leads to offspring.

The second aspect: that maleness is the seat of acting, and femaleness is the seat of being acted upon. When the male becomes the one acted upon and the female the actor, that is contrary to the requirement of nature and the reverse of divine wisdom.

The third aspect: occupying oneself with mere desire is resemblance to the beast. And if occupation with desire yields a benefit other than satisfying desire, then satisfying desire with a woman yields another benefit beyond satisfying desire, namely the existence of offspring and the preservation of the human species, which is the noblest of species. As for satisfying desire with a male, it yields nothing but the mere satisfaction of desire, so that is resemblance to animals and departure from the human disposition, and so it is at the utmost of ugliness.

The fourth aspect: suppose the doer takes pleasure in that act; still, it entails great shame and complete defect for the one acted upon, in a way that this defect never leaves him for all eternity, and the intelligent person does not accept, for the sake of a base pleasure that ends at once, the imposition of a lasting defect upon another.

The fifth aspect: it is an act that entails the consolidation of enmity between the doer and the one acted upon, and perhaps this leads the one acted upon to kill the doer because his nature recoils at seeing him, or to strive to harm him by every means he can. As for the occurrence of this act between a man and a woman, it entails the consolidation of affection and love and the attainment of great benefits, as He, exalted, said: ﴿He created for you mates from yourselves that you may find tranquility in them, and placed between you affection and mercy﴾ [al-Rum: 21].

The sixth aspect: He, exalted, placed in the womb a strong power of drawing in the semen, so when a man has intercourse with a woman, the drawing power is strong, and no part of the semen remains in the passages but is expelled. As for when he has intercourse with a male, there is in that specific organ of the one acted upon no drawing power for the semen, and then the drawing is not complete, so some parts of the semen remain in those passages and are not expelled, and they rot and spoil, and from them arise severe swellings and great diseases. This is a benefit that cannot be known except through medical laws.

These are the aspects that necessitate the ugliness of this act. I have seen some who were weak in religion saying: He, exalted, said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their spouses or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 5-6], and this requires the permissibility of intercourse with a slave absolutely, whether male or female. He said: It cannot be said that we specify this generality by His saying: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 165] and His saying: ﴿Do you commit the abomination which no one among the worlds has preceded you in?﴾ He said: Because each of these two verses is more general than the other in one respect and more specific in another respect, since the slave may be male or female, and also the male may be a slave or not a slave. Given that this is the case, specifying one by the other is no more appropriate than the reverse. The preference lies on this side, because His saying: ﴿except from their spouses or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 6] is the law of Muhammad, while the story of Lot is the law of the other prophets, and the law of Muhammad (ﷺ) is more worthy than the law of those prophets who preceded him. Also, the basic principle in benefits and pleasures is permissibility, and also ownership grants absolute right of disposal. I said to him: Argument is accepted only where there is room for doubt, and it has been established by manifest mass transmission from the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ) that this act is forbidden, with strong emphasis on its prohibition, and argument, when it is raised against a mass-transmitted text, is invalid.

Then God, exalted, said, relating about Lot that he said to them: ﴿Rather, you are a people who exceed limits.﴾ The meaning is as if he said to them: You are excessive in all deeds, so it is not far from you that you also undertake this excess.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 7, verse 82:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel them from your city; indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure."﴾

What is meant by this is: expel Lut and his followers. This is because He, may He be exalted, said in another surah: ﴿Expel the family of Lut from your city; indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure.﴾ [An-Naml: 56] Also, because the apparent meaning is that they only strove to expel the one who forbade them from the act they desired and wanted, and that forbidder was none other than Lut and his people. Regarding His saying ﴿they keep themselves pure﴾ there are several aspects:

The first: that this act is a dealing with the place of impurity, so whoever abandons it has become pure.

The second: that distance from sin is called purity, so His saying ﴿they keep themselves pure﴾ means they keep far away from sins and transgressions.

The third: that they only said ﴿they are men who keep themselves pure﴾ in mockery of them and of their purity from immoralities, just as the wicked among the debauched say to some of the righteous when they admonish them: "Keep this ascetic away from us, and relieve us of this self-denier."

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 7, verses 83–84:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.﴾ ﴿And We rained upon them a rain. So see how was the end of the criminals.﴾

Know that His saying ﴿So We saved him and his family﴾ may mean by "his family" his helpers and followers who accepted his religion, and it may mean those related to him by lineage. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the intended ones are his two daughters. As for His saying ﴿except his wife﴾, that is, his spouse. It is said "the man's wife" meaning his spouse, and it is said "the woman's husband" meaning her spouse; this is because the husband stands in the position of owner of her, while the woman does not stand in the position of owner of the man. So when the woman is attributed to the man by the general term, marriage and the ownership of marriage are known, and when the man is attributed to the woman by the general term, marriage is known.

As for His saying ﴿she was among those who remained behind﴾: it is said "the thing ghabara yaghburu ghuburan" when it lingered and remained. Al-Hudhali said:

"So I lingered after them in a toilsome life, and I think that I am a follower who will be overtaken."

He means: I remained. So the meaning of the verse is that she was among those who remained behind from salvation, that is, among those who stayed behind and did not attain salvation. It is said: "So-and-so ghabara this matter," meaning he did not attain it. It is also permissible that the intended meaning is that she did not travel with Lot and his family, but lagged behind him and remained in that place, which is the place of punishment.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾. It is said "matarat al-sama'" and "amtarat," and the first is more eloquent; and "amtarahum mataran wa ʿadhaban," and likewise "amtara ʿalayhim." The intended meaning is that He, exalted, rained upon them stones from the sky, by the evidence that He said in another verse: ﴿And We rained upon them stones of sijjil﴾ [al-Hijr: 74].

* * *

Then He said: ﴿So see how was the end of the criminals﴾. In it are two issues:

The first issue: the apparent wording, although it is addressed specifically to the Messenger, peace be upon him, the intended meaning is all those who are responsible, so that they may take warning from it and be restrained.

If it is said: how can they take warning from it when they are secure from the punishment of annihilation?

We say: the punishment of the Hereafter is greater and more lasting than that. So upon hearing this story, they recall the punishment of the Hereafter, reproaching themselves over the punishment of annihilation, and this becomes a deterrent and a warning.

The second issue: the position of al-Shafiʿi, may Allah be pleased with him, is that sodomy entails the hadd punishment, while Abu Hanifa said it does not entail it. Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, may argue from this verse in several respects:

First: it is established in the sharia of Lot, peace be upon him, that the sodomite is to be stoned, and the basic principle regarding what is established is its continuance, unless the arrival of an abrogating ruling becomes evident. No abrogating ruling for this rule appeared in the sharia of Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, so it is necessary to affirm its continuance.

Second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [al-Anʿam: 90]. We have already explained in the commentary of this verse that it indicates that the law of those before us is a proof for us.

Third: He, exalted, said: ﴿So see how was the end of the criminals﴾, and the apparent meaning is that by this end is meant what was mentioned before, namely the sending down of stones upon them, and by "the criminals" are meant those who do the deed of the people of Lot; because that is what was mentioned previously, so it is directed to it. Thus the meaning of the verse becomes: see how Allah rained stones upon those who do that specific deed.

Mentioning a ruling immediately after a fitting attribute indicates that this attribute is the cause (ʿillah) of that ruling. So this verse requires that this specific crime be the cause of the occurrence of this specific deterrent, and when the cause is established, this ruling must occur wherever this cause occurs.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 7, verse 85:

[Page 141]
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Midian [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. There has already come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So give full measure and weight, and do not deprive people of their due, and do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation. That is better for you, if you are believers."﴾

Know that this is the fifth story. We have mentioned that the implied sense is: "And We sent to Midian their brother Shu'ayb." We have also mentioned that this brotherhood was one of lineage, not of religion, and we have mentioned the aspects of this. Scholars differed about Midian: it was said that it is the name of the town, and it was said that it is the name of the tribe, because they are the descendants of Midian ibn Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and "Madyan" became the name of the tribe, just as one says "Bakr" and "Tamim." Shu'ayb is among his descendants, namely: Shu'ayb ibn Nuwayb ibn Madyan ibn Ibrahim, the Friend of the All-Merciful.

Know that He, exalted is He, related of Shu'ayb that he commanded his people in this verse concerning several matters:

The first: he commanded them to worship Allah and forbade them from worshipping other than Allah. This is a principle upheld in the laws of all the prophets. So he said: ﴿Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him.﴾

The second: he claimed prophethood, saying: ﴿There has already come to you clear evidence from your Lord.﴾ The "clear evidence" here must mean a miracle, since a claimant to prophethood必 must have one; otherwise he would be a pretender rather than a prophet. So this verse indicates that he was given a miracle confirming his truthfulness. As to what kind of miracle it was, the Qur'an gives no indication of it, just as the Qur'an does not indicate many of the miracles of our Messenger.

The author of al-Kashshaf said: Among the miracles of Shu'ayb: he gave his staff to Moses, and that staff fought the serpent. Also, he told Moses: "These sheep will bear young, some black and some white, and I have given them to you," and it happened as he had reported. Then he said: These circumstances were miracles of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, because Moses at that time had not claimed the message.

Know that this statement is based on a principle on which our companions and the Mu'tazilah differ. For we hold that one who afterwards becomes a prophet and messenger may be shown by God various kinds of miracles before the conveyance of revelation, and this is called "irhas" (a preparatory sign) of prophethood. Such irhas is permissible according to us, but not permissible according to the Mu'tazilah. So the circumstances related by the author of al-Kashshaf are, according to us, irhasat for Moses, peace be upon him, while according to the Mu'tazilah they are miracles of Shu'ayb, since irhas is impermissible in their view.

The third: he said: ﴿So give full measure and weight.﴾

Know that it is the custom of the prophets, peace be upon them, that when they see their people inclined toward one kind of corruption more than toward the rest, they begin by forbidding them from that kind. The people of Shu'ayb were addicted to cheating and short-measuring, so for this reason he began by mentioning this matter, saying: ﴿So give full measure and weight.﴾ Here there are two questions.

First question: the fa' in his saying ﴿So give full measure﴾ requires that the command to give full measure be, as it were, a consequence and result of what was previously mentioned, namely his saying: ﴿There has already come to you clear evidence from your Lord.﴾ So what is the connection here?

The answer: It is as if he says: cheating and short-measuring are a term for betrayal in a small thing, and it is an act that is abhorrent to the intellects; and in addition, clear evidence and the law which makes it forbidden have come, so you have no excuse in it. ﴿So give full measure.﴾

Second question: Why did he say "al-kayl wal-mizan" (the measure and the weight) and not "al-mikyal wal-mizan" (the measuring vessel and the weight), as in Surah Hud?

The answer: By "al-kayl" he meant the instrument of measuring, which is the mikyal; or what is measured with it is called "al-kayl," just as one says "al-ʿaysh" (the livelihood) for that by which one lives.

The fourth: his saying: ﴿and do not deprive people of their due.﴾ The meaning is that, when he forbade his people from cheating in measure and weight, he then forbade them from cheating and diminishing in every way. This includes the prohibition of usurpation, theft, taking bribes, highway robbery, and seizing property by means of stratagems.

The fifth: his saying: ﴿and do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation.﴾ This is because taking people's property without their consent necessarily produces dispute and enmity, and these two necessarily produce corruption. Therefore he said after it: ﴿and do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation.﴾ The explanation of this phrase has already passed, and they mentioned several aspects of it. It was said: ﴿do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾ by undertaking cheating in measure and weight, because that is followed by corruption. It was said: he meant by it the prohibition of everything that is corruption, taking the word in its general sense. It was said: his saying ﴿and do not deprive people of their due﴾ is a prohibition of the corruptions of this world, and his saying ﴿and do not cause corruption on the earth﴾ is a prohibition of the corruptions of religion, so that the verse comprises the prohibition of the corruptions of both this world and religion. They differed about the meaning of ﴿after its reformation.﴾ It was said: after the earth had been reformed by the coming of the Prophet, after it had been corrupt through being devoid of him; so He forbade them from corruption, now that it had become righteous. It was said: the meaning is that you should not cause corruption after God has reformed it by increasing blessings among you. The essence of these five obligations returns to two principles: exalting the command of Allah, which includes affirming the Oneness of God and prophethood; and compassion toward the creation of Allah, which includes abstaining from cheating and from corruption. Their essence returns to abstaining from harming others, as if He, exalted is He, were saying: bringing benefit to all is impossible, but restraining harm from all is possible. Then, when He, exalted is He, mentioned these five, He said: ﴿That﴾, which refers to these five, and the meaning is: "better for you in the Hereafter, if you are believers in the Hereafter." The intended meaning is that abstaining from cheating and abstaining from corruption is better for you in seeking wealth, in meaning; for when people know from you fulfillment, truthfulness and trustworthiness, they will be eager to deal with you, and your wealth will increase. ﴿If you are believers﴾, that is: if you are those who affirm me in what I say.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 7, verses 86–87:

Allah's words: ﴿And do not sit at every path, threatening and turning away from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few and He multiplied you. And observe how was the end of the corrupters.﴾ ﴿And if there is a group among you who believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who did not believe, then be patient until Allah judges between us. And He is the best of judges.﴾

Know that Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) added to the five obligations mentioned earlier several other matters:

The first: He forbade them from sitting on the paths of the religion and the methods of truth, so that they would prevent people from accepting it.

Regarding His words ﴿And do not sit at every path﴾ there are two opinions:

The first: "path" is understood as the road that people travel. It is narrated that they used to sit on the roads and frighten those who believed in Shu'ayb (peace be upon him).

The second: "path" is understood as the methods of the religion. The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Kashshaf) said: ﴿And do not sit at every path﴾ means: do not follow Satan in his words: ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾ [Al-A'raf: 16]. He said: "By the path is meant everything that is among the methods of the religion. The proof that the path means this is His words: ﴿and turning away from the way of Allah﴾."

His words ﴿at every path﴾ are said in the form: qa'ada lahu bi-makani kadha, wa-'ala makani kadha, wa-fi makani kadha (he sat for him at such a place, on such a place, in such a place). These prepositions interchange in these contexts because their meanings are close. When you say qa'ada bi-makani kadha, the bā' (bi-) indicates attachment (li-l-ilsaq), and he has attached himself to that place.

* * *

As for His words ﴿threatening﴾, its position (mahall) and the position of what is conjoined to it is the accusative of circumstance (al-nasb 'ala al-hal). The sense is: "Do not sit threatening, nor turning away from the way of Allah, nor seeking to make it crooked in the way of Allah." The summary is that He forbade them from sitting on the path of Allah while occupied with any of these three matters. Know that when He conjoined some of these three to others, it became necessary that they be different from each other. So His words ﴿threatening﴾ refer to inflicting harms upon them. As for turning away, it may occur by threatening with harms, it may occur by promising benefits in return for abandoning the faith, and it may occur by preventing him from going to the Messenger to hear his speech.

As for His words ﴿and seeking to make it crooked﴾, the intended meaning is casting doubts and dubious claims. The meaning of the verse is that Shu'ayb forbade the people from preventing others from accepting the true religion by any of these three methods. If you reflect, you will know that no one can prevent another from accepting a doctrine or a saying except by one of these three methods.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And remember when you were few and He multiplied you.﴾ The purpose of this is that when they remember the abundance of Allah's favours upon them, it is apparent that this moves them to obedience and to keeping away from disobedience. Al-Zajjaj said: "This statement admits three aspects: He multiplied your number after being few; He multiplied you with wealth after poverty; and He multiplied you with power after weakness." The reasoning is that if they were poor or weak, they were like the few, in that no strength or might came from their existence. As for the multiplication of their number after fewness, it is that Madyan ibn Ibrahim married Rithā bint Lūṭ, and she bore children until their number grew.

Then after this He said: ﴿And observe how was the end of the corrupters.﴾ The meaning is: remember the end of the corrupters and what disgrace and punishment befell them, so that this serves as a deterrent for you from disobedience and corruption. So His words ﴿And remember when you were few and He multiplied you﴾ are intended to show that when they remember Allah's blessings upon them, they submit and obey. And His words ﴿And observe how was the end of the corrupters﴾ are intended to show that when they know that the end of the corrupting rebels is nothing but disgrace and punishment, they guard against corruption and disobedience and obey. Thus the purpose of these two statements is to move them to obedience first by way of encouragement, and then by way of warning.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And if there is a group among you who believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who did not believe, then be patient﴾. The purpose of this is to console the hearts of the believers and to deter those who did not believe, because His words ﴿then be patient﴾ are a threat. Likewise His words ﴿until Allah judges between us.﴾ The intended meaning is the elevation of the ranks of the believers and the manifestation of the humiliation of the disbelievers. This condition may appear in this world, and if it does not appear in this world, then it must appear in the Hereafter.

[p. 144]

Then He said: ﴿And He is the best of judges.﴾ That is, He is a Judge who is exempt from injustice, partiality and oppression. So He must single out the believing, God-fearing person with lofty ranks, and the wretched disbeliever with various kinds of punishment. A parallel to this is His words: ﴿Shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth?﴾ [Sad: 28].
